sentences.text: This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 23.09.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.808/2016, on the file of the IInd Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts:
2. On 26.11.2015, the claimant and his son had been to M.H.Pattana for mason work and after completion of their work in order to return to their house, they were standing near M.H.Pattana Gate at about 4.00 p.m., and at that point of time a Honda Shine Motor Bike bearing registration No.KA.01.EV.9069 came from Gubbi side in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed the claimant.

As a result,
he suffered injuries.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part,
and awarded a compensation of Rs.2,83,514/-, along with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent No.2 therein, liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
5.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:

3. Food and Nourishment : Rs. 10,000/-
4. Transportation Charges : Rs. 10,000/-
5. Loss Of Amenities : Rs. 25,000/-
6. Loss of Future Income : Rs. 1,26,000/-

8. Loss of income during : Rs. 22,500/-

Future Medical Expenses : Rs. 20,000/-
TOTAL : Rs. 2,83,514/-
6.

It is seen from the medical evidence on record, viz., Exhibit-P5 which is Wound Certificate and Exhibit-P7 which is discharge report, that the claimant has suffered, Comminuted Right Patella Fracture.
The said injury is grievous in nature.
The claimant was working as a Mason.
The accident has occurred on 26.11.2015.
The Tribunal has taken notional income of Rs.7,500/- per month, which is on lesser side.
Therefore, as per Chart of notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month is to be taken as notional monthly income of the claimant.
The claimant was aged 45 years and was working as Mason and the Doctor has stated that the claimant has 30% to right lower limb and 10% to the whole-body.
Therefore, on this the compensation needs to be enhanced.
7. Further, the claimant was admitted to hospital for 60 days as inpatient.
The quantum of compensation awarded under the pain and suffering, food and nourishment, loss of amenities in life, loss of future income, attendant charges are all on lesser side.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained, disability occurred, coupled with the nature of avocation this Court is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an additional sum of Rs.65,000/- along with interest @
6% per annum from the date of the petition till the realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Therefore, the appellant-claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,48,514/- as against Rs.2,83,514/-.

The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.65,000/-
(Rs.3,48,514 - Rs.2,83,514) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

ORDER i.
The appeal is Allowed In Part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 23.09.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.808/2016, on the file of the IInd Additional District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tumakuru is modified to the aforesaid extent.

iii. The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.65,000/- (Rs.3,48,514 - Rs.2,83,514) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iv. The remaining observations and findings made by the Tribunal in the aforesaid impugned judgment and award are kept in tact.
